headline: The late-2023 starting point
summary: A useful family shortlist anchor with a published three-seat test. Check the actual build and restraint combination before buying.

range.basis: WLTP combined; original Australian RWD claim

battery.basis: Tesla did not publish pack capacity in the Australian launch specification

consumption.basis: Observed 2023 CarExpert mixed urban/suburban/freeway test; not WLTP or a promise for your use

acCharging.basis: Tesla Australia onboard limit at 400 V three-phase 16 A; single-phase 32 A supply is 7.4 kW. Check vehicle touchscreen limit.

dcCharging.basis: Reported peak, not sustained charging power

chargeTime: Australian road test reports roughly 18–20 min to 80% at a suitable fast charger; starting charge and conditions vary.

boot.basis: Tesla own cargo measure behind second row, seats up; not stated as VDA; excludes 117 L front boot; not directly comparable with VDA figures

bootAllRows.basis: Tesla own cargo measure behind second row, seats up; not stated as VDA; excludes 117 L front boot; not directly comparable with VDA figures

length.basis: Original-generation Tesla owner manual; approximate overall length

width.basis: Tesla body width excluding mirrors; 1978 mm is folded-mirror width, not body width

towing.basis: Not verified for this Australian configuration

warranty: Originally 4 years / 80,000 km; check the remaining original cover. The 2026 warranty is not retroactive.
batteryWarranty: 8 years / 160,000 km with minimum 70% capacity retention; original terms apply.
servicing: No compulsory annual service in the Australian road test; inspect the vehicle-specific maintenance schedule.

safety.applicability: Original five-seat Australian-delivered variants, built February 2022–April 2025.

familyFit.summary: BabyDrive fitted a named three-restraint combination to a 2023 car; your own seats are unconfirmed.
familyFit.row2: Two outer ISOFIX positions; top tether on all three rear backrests.
familyFit.row3: No third row on this five-seat configuration.
familyFit.testedSeats: 2023 test: rear-facing InfaSecure Attain More plus forward-facing Achieve More and Attain More; an alternative two Achieve More plus one Attain More also fitted.
familyFit.buckleAccess: Independent test did not establish fit or daily buckle access for your three boosters. ANCAP could not correctly install its Type A capsule and one selected booster in the centre position; its tests assess each restraint separately, not three together.
familyFit.access: Flat rear floor helps moving between positions.
familyFit.ventilation: Rear console vents; verify airflow with your restraints fitted.

pros: Published three-across restraint evidence.
BabyDrive fitted a twin pram with shopping alongside.
Observed mixed-driving efficiency provides a transparent cost example.
cons: Original general warranty is relatively short.
No verified VDA boot figure in this dataset.
Three boosters can need different buckle space from harnessed seats.
inspection: Trial all three restraints together and check every buckle with the children seated.
Confirm VIN, build date, service history, recall completion and remaining warranty.
For a late-2023 listing, record build and delivery dates; ask Tesla to confirm suspension hardware and inspect the actual interior.
Confirm the VIN is clear of outstanding REC-006300 power-steering software action.

changes.text: The October 2023 ambient-light/dashboard update was reported for China with Australian availability unconfirmed; do not infer Australian equipment from the China announcement.
Juniper changes body/interior and has separate restraint-test and ANCAP evidence; see the separate entry.

gaps: Exact Australian comfort-suspension cutover and late-2023 hardware are not verified by VIN.
Pack gross/usable capacity and a VDA-comparable boot measure remain unverified.
2025 pre-refresh stock must be identified by body/build date; not included in this year group.

cons: Above the target budget as a new car.

Confirm VIN, build date, service history, recall completion and remaining warranty.

headline: Great value; a tight three-seat brief
summary: Affordable used-EV context, but the published family test flags shoulder-width limits for three forward-facing restraints.

battery.basis: Published manufacturer pack capacity; usable/gross split not stated; confirm early build

consumption.basis: Not verified for this Australian configuration

chargeTime: Australian review quotes about 35 min for 10–80% on a suitable DC charger; conditions vary.

bootAllRows.basis: Manufacturer rear luggage claim, rear seats up; measurement standard unspecified

width.basis: Manufacturer overall body width; mirrors not included

servicing: Current BYD guide: 12 months / 20,000 km; original schedule and early check requirements must be confirmed.

safety.applicability: Australian Standard/Extended built from 21 November 2022; earlier cars only after the prescribed child-restraint anchorage updates.

familyFit.summary: BabyDrive’s 2024 combination fitted, but the reviewer reported insufficient shoulder room for three forward-facing seats.

familyFit.row3: No third row on this five-seat configuration.

familyFit.access: No third row to spread the restraints across.

Compact exterior with rear vents and a flat rear floor.

Confirm VIN, build date, service history, recall completion and remaining warranty.
On a 2022 car, obtain evidence that the Australian child-restraint anchorage updates were completed.

Essential/Premium naming and later EVO are separate entries; do not use this original-body fit result as evidence for EVO.

gaps: Standard-range pack appears as 49.94 kWh in one review versus 49.92 in the manufacturer reference; use VIN-specific documents.
Comparable rated consumption not confirmed; energy-cost estimate withheld.
